Commentary.Commentary: The wickets were evenly shared by the Windies bowlers. Kemar Roach and Shannon Gabriel picked a couple apiece while Miguel Cummins got rid of the last three. They didn't allow the visitors any breathing space at any time of this innings. Dinesh Chandimal and Dickwella were the only two who showed some determination. Besides that, there was nothing to write about. 42 extras being the second highest contributor in their innings which goes on to show how poorly they batted. The Windies are well and truly dominating the proceedings. They will come out with the intention of playing sensible cricket while Sri Lanka will look to keep a tight lid on the scoring and get some early wickets. Join us back in a while for the final session of the day.

NEWS IS WEST INDIES HAVEN'T ENFORCED THE FOLLOW-ON. The home team will walk out to bat with a first innings lead of 229 runs. The first line is indicative of how dominating they were with the ball. This session started with Niroshan Dickwella gifting his wicket away through a poor run out and after which, the lower order simply failed to get going. They lost their last five wickets for just 45 runs. AN EARLY TEA HAS BEEN CALLED, so the home team will start their second essay with the bat after the break.

OUT! That is it for the Sri Lankan innings, they have been BOWLED OUT FOR 185! Cummins gets his third. Another short ball on middle, Kumara like he has been doing goes for another pull. The ball takes the top edge and goes high up in the air towards fine leg. The keeper turns, runs towards the ball and takes it on the second attempt.
NO BALL AND FOUR! Kumara is not going to die wondering here. He backs away to a length ball on middle and slaps it through mid on for a boundary. Also the bowler has overstepped again.
Bumper, the batsman misses the pull shot.
Goes fuller this time. Kumara drives it to covers.
NO BALL! Extra number 41! Cummins once again bangs it short. The batsman goes for the pull but misses. The bowler oversteps.
FOUR! Again handy runs these! Another short ball, the batsman takes on the challenge of pulling it. The ball takes the top edge and goes over the slip cordon for a boundary.
Very full on middle, defended.
Flighted ball on middle, Gamage lunges and blocks it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Loopy ball on off, the batsman keeps it out.
Floats it up on middle, it is kept out.
Tosses this one up on off, it is kept out.
A bumper to end the over on middle, Kumara mistimes his pull to mid-wicket.
Short ball aimed at the rib cage of the batsman. Kumara somehow manages to keep it out.
Back of a length on middle, the batsman defends it onto the ground.
Lahiru Kumara strides out to the middle.

OUT! Cummins has the last laugh! It is another bouncer which rushes onto the batsman. Lakmal once again goes for the pull shot which has given him quite a few runs in this innings. This time though he mistimes it towards mid-wicket. Bishoo there accepts an easy catch.
Goes fuller this time on off, Lakmal whose weight is on the back foot somehow manages to keep it out.
FOUR! That has been pulled with disdain! This is short and on middle, Lakmal picks the length early and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. 40 more to avoid the follow-on.
He does so! Very full on middle, the batsman plays it out to point.
Eases it down to long off and gets to the other end. Gamage has one ball to play out now.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Slower and on the shorter side. Lakmal whips it but the ball hits the man at short leg.
Loopy ball on off, the batsman defends it.
Flatter on middle, Lakmal works it through mid-wicket and bags two. Handy runs these for Sri Lanka.
Back of a length on off, Gamage defends it onto the ground.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and lets it through to the keeper.
Shortish again on the body of the batsman. Lakmal once again plays the pull shot but to the man at fine leg for a run.
SIX! Top edge and all the way! Lakmal is now looking to play some shots. He gets a short ball outside off, Lakmal goes for the pull but gets a top edge which flies over the keeper  for a biggie.
Shorter in length on middle, Lakmal tries to pull but mistimes it to mid-wicket.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.

FIVE WIDES! This is way outside off and swinging away further. The batsman lets it be. The keeper dives to his right but only manages to get a hand to it. It races to the third man fence. The umpire also signals a wide.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Lahiru Gamage is the next man in.

OUT! BISHOO STRIKES! He has bowled well so far and he gets his reward. Bowls the slider on middle, Dilruwan prods forward and plays for the away turn but the ball goes on with the arm and it takes the inside edge. Hits the pads and goes into the hands of short leg. Shai Hope there takes an easy catch. The end now is nigh for Sri Lanka.
Flatter on middle, Perera defends it off the back foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy ball on off, Perera defends it onto the ground.
SIX! Dilruwan says enough of the defensive strokes! Bishoo tosses this up on off, Perera's eyes lit up there. He clears his front leg and lofts it over the long on fence for a biggie.
Shortish and on off, Lakmal pushes it to point.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
Bowls it a touch short and outside off, Lakmal goes after it with a cut shot but does not connect.
Bowls it on the pads, Lakmal tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
A good bumper on middle, Lakmal does well to evade it.
Angles it into the batsman. Lakmal works it to the man at short leg.
Drinks break.
Floated delivery on the off, the batsman comes on the front foot and dabs it to cover-point.
Quicker on middle and leg, the batsman works it against the spin on the leg side for a single.
Pushes it through and the batsman pushes it to mid off. Can't find the gap.
Third defensive stroke on the trot from Suranga Lakmal.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Loopy delivery from Bishoo outside off, the batsman leans on the front foot and defends it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Big shout for the fielders but the umpire is unmoved. Good length ball on off, angling in from outside off, Perera is hit on the pads as he plays at it. Impact seems to be pretty high.
Ball hits the batsman low on the pads.
Drifting it down the leg side, the batsman looks to flick that but misses. It goes off the pads on the leg side for a leg bye.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Suranga Lakmal strides out to bat.

OUT! GONE! The short ball does the trick. Herath is a compulsive puller and this time it proves to be his undoing. A well-directed bumper from Miguel Cummins, it gets big on the batsman. The left-hander still goes for the pull but ends up mistiming it. The ball balloons towards the mid-wicket region. Hetmyer (sub) there runs in a few steps and takes a simple catch. Hang on! The umpire wants to check for the front foot no ball, has the bowler overstepped? Nope. He has got something behind the line and it is enough to deem it legitimate.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Missed stumping? Maybe! Perera is foxed by the length of it. He steps out and aims to defend that but gets hit on the pads and the ball rolls to the keeper, who fails to gather it cleanly. The batsman came back quickly but the keeper definetly had a chance there.
Pushes it quicker through the air, Dilruwan defends it out.
Flatter ball outside off, the batsman chops it to cover-point.
Slider on the middle and leg stump line, Perera pushes it back to the bowler.
On a good length from Cummins, the batsman pushes it to backward point.

Good nut from Cummins, he finally gets one to pitch in the right zone and gets some purchase of the deck. The ball moves away a little after pitching, Herath looks to punch that but he is beaten for the away movement.
Short delivery but falsely directed. The batsman ducks under it with absolute ease.
Drifting down leg, Perera goes back to glance that but he misses it and the ball rolls off the thigh pad to fine leg for a leg bye.
On a good length outside off, the right-hander doesn't offer stroke to it.
Starts with an ill directed delivery, bowls it full and down the leg side. The batsman looks to glance that but misses it.
Miguel Cummins is back into the attack.
Tossed up delivery outside off, the batsman lunges on the front foot and defends it on the pitch.
The batsman plays a sweep shot to the square leg region.

Tossed up delivery from Bishoo outside off, spins in a little. Herath goes for the sweep but gets hit on the pads. There is an appeal for an LBW but the umpire isn't interested. Impact was well outside edge and that's another good call from the on-field umpire.
Fires it flat on off, Herath defends it down the track.
Spinning in from outside off and it hits the pads of Herath as he looks to defend that.
Loopy delivery outside off, the batsman plays a reverse sweep past short third man. They collect a couple more.
Sharp bumper from Gabriel to end the over, the batsman leaves it alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Uppish... it lands safely though. Short ball, Herath goes for the pull, but ends up splicing it to the vacant square leg region. Single.
Attacks the leg stump line, Herath looks to flick that but misses it and gets pinged on the pads.
A wide delivery on off, the batsman opens the face of the bat and guides it past gully for a brace.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.

Was there a run out opportunity? Oh yes. Herath dabs it to backward point and calls for a quick single. His partner sends him back, but he is slow in returning. Luckily for Herath, the throw from the fielder is wayward and he survives.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter ball, the batsman chops it past the first slip fielder for a single.
Perera goes right back and defends it on the off side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Rangana Herath is the next man in.

OUT! That is pretty clumsy from Dickwella but the Windies won't complain as they have got the bonus breakthrough. Getting run out in Test cricket is criminal but the way he got out is just awful. Another set batsman for Sri Lanka departs, the visitors are in a big hole. Let me explain what happened in that delivery first. Flatter ball from Bishoo and the batsman works it down the track. The bowler tries to stop it and creates the confusion. The batsmen eventually decide to go through. However, Brathwaite from mid-wicket runs towards the ball and hits the stumps at the bowler's end. The wicket-keeper batsman didn't rush as he didn't expect the throw to come his way. There is an appeal for a run out and the TV umpire has been referred. Replays show that the batsman is well short. Sri Lanka have lost their sixth wicket and they still trail by 274 runs.
Direct hit and the case has been sent upstairs. Dickwella is the man in question. Seems like he is well short. Dear oh dear, this is pretty sloppy from the wicket-keeper batsman.
Seam up delivery from Gabriel, it moves away a little. Perera doesn't offer a stroke to it.
Gabriel attacks the pads, Dickwella uses his wrists as he glances it to fine leg for a single.
Fuller length ball on the stumps, the batsman forces it down the track.
Jumps right across his stumps and works that delivery from Gabriel to mid-wicket.
Drops it short again, angling in, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
Angling in from outside off, the batsman moves across and taps it to mid on.
Floats it outside off, Dilruwan pushes it towards cover-point.
Drifting in from outside off and the batsman drives it back to the leggie.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Much flatter and quicker from Bishoo, the batsman punches it to long on for a single.
Dickwella plays a sweep but it goes off the bottom edge to Holder at leg slip.
Shortens his length and the batsman is quick to spot that. Goes right back and pushes it to mid off. It goes straight to the fielder.
Tests the batsman with a bumper, Perera goes down and lets it be.
False shot from Dickwella, he plays away from the body and gets a thick inside edge which rolls down to fine leg. Single taken.
Drifting it down leg, the ball brushes the pads of Dickwella and goes through to the keeper. Gabriel has overstepped and there is a signal for no ball from Aleem Dar.
A widish delivery from Gabriel and Dickwella tries to cash in. He plays a drive but toe ends it to mid off.
Incoming delivery from the bowler, Perera goes for the drive but it goes off the inner half towards square leg. They steal a quick single.
Another quick delivery, at 142 clicks, the batsman looks to flick that but gets rapped on the pads.
Pacey delivery from Gabriel, on a length and it zooms in sharply, Perera covers his stumps and leaves it calmly.
Spins down leg and the batsman misses it on the pads as he looks to work that.
Fuller ball from Bishoo, defended by the batsman.
Flatter from Bishoo, the batsman sits back and cuts it to deep point for a single. The two batsmen nearly collided mid-pitch and hence they could only manage a single.
Eases it in the gap on the off side and gets off strike with a single.
The batsman steps out and pushes it down the track. Bishoo rushes to his left and makes a good stop.
Loopy delivery, it spins in from outside off. Dickwella defends it watchfully.
Uses his wrists and flicks it through mid-wicket. A couple more pocketed by Perera.
Short of a length ball, angling into the batsman. Perera defends but it goes off the inner half on the leg side.
FOUR! Great strike, much better from the shot he played off the first ball. Another overpitched delivery. This time, Perera gets closer to the pitch of it and drills it through covers for a boundary.
On a good length outside off, the batsman doens't play at it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.

Dropped by Chase! Second catch shelled off Gabriel's bowling in this innings. A reckless shot by Dilruwan Perera to say the least, he is the last accomplished batsman in the line-up and he needs to play a little more selectively. It is a fullish delivery outside off from the bowler and the batsman slices it carelessly towards backward point. Roston stays low and gets both the hands to it but fails to hang on. The pacer is absolutely livid seeing that.
Shannon Gabriel will continue from the other end.
Pushes it much flatter on this occasion and the batsman defends it on the off side.
Spins it in from outside off, Dickwella works it with the turn towards mid-wicket.
Loopy ball on the stumps from Bishoo, the left-hander defends it out.
Spinning into the pads, Dickwella goes back to glance that but misses.
Flatter from Bishoo on middle and leg, the batsman taps it to the short leg fielder.
Drops it short on the stumps, Dickwella backs away and forces it through the covers for a brace. A positive start from the wicket-keeper batsman.

Welcome back. Players are taking their positions. Niroshan Dickwella and Dilruwan Perera will resume their innings, the former will be on strike. For the Windies team, Devendra Bishoo will start the proceedings.
... Day 3, Session 2...

It could have been Sri Lanka's session but the wicket of Dinesh Chandimal has pushed them back again. The traveling team were jolted early this morning as they lost Roshen Silva. However, a 78-run union between Dinesh Chandimal and Niroshan Dickwella gave them the hope of putting a fightback. The bowling attack of the home team didn't look penetrative during that phase. Sri Lanka were looking good to pocket the session, but theie skipper played a loose shot prior to Lunch and gift wrapped his wicket to the Windies. The visitors still trail by a huge margin and they will be hoping for their tail to wag and do what the lower-order of the opposition did. While, the West Indies team will come all guns blazing after the break with an aim to wrap the innings quickly. Join us back in a while for the afternoon session.
Delivers it fuller on the stumps to end the over, Perera blocks it solidly down the track. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 3.
Much fuller from Gabriel and Perera powers it through mid on. A couple more to the right-hander.
Dipping in sharply from outside off, the batsman covers his stumps and lets it through.
Bowls it on a length outside off and the batsman decides to leave it.
Incoming delivery on the stumps and the batsman whips it through mid on for a brace.

OUT! Taken at backward point! Oh dear, the Sri Lankan skipper has thrown it away, he will be kicking himself after playing that shot. The traveling team still need 93 runs to avoid the follow-on. It is a nothing delivery from Gabriel, short and wide asking to be punished. The batsman rocks back and slaps it hard but he fails to keep it down. It goes straight into the hands of Chase at backward point. The fielder there takes a sharp catch and that ends a 78-run union. West Indies will be really happy to see the back of the visiting skipper who looked in good nick. Just at the stroke of lunch, the hosts have got the important breakthrough. Dilruwan Perera walks out to bat.
Shannon Gabriel comes back into the attack.
Pushes it quicker through the air. Delivered at 82 kph. Dickwella defends it off the back foot.
Makes room by backing away, cuts it through the covers for a single.
Hint of turn for Bishoo! Flatter leg break on middle, spins away a little. Chandimal sits back and negotiates it safely.
Slider from Bishoo, on middle and leg. The batsman defends it out.
Loopy ball from Bishoo, Dickwella takes it on the full and paddles it away to fine leg for a single.
Guides it right between the two men on the off side. They steal a quick single.
Bowls it much fuller and the batsman drives, only to find the fielder at covers.
Roach oversteps and an extra conceded! It's a fuller length ball on the stumps, Dickwella pushes it on the leg side.
Fullish delivery on off, the batsman drives on the up to short extra cover.
Bowls from the edge of the crease, short and down the leg side. Dickwella goes for the pull but fails to connect.
Looks repeat the shot off the previous ball but doesn't get the timing right on this occasion.

FOUR! Lovely cover drive from Dickwella, timing and placement were simply spot on! Fuller length ball from Roach outside off, the batsman comes on the front foot and strikes it on the up through the gap for a boundary.
Overpitched delivery on off, Dickwella plays a drive but it goes off the toe end to mid off.
Drops it short outside off, Chandimal cuts it to cover-point, but can't find the gap.
Tossed up delivery on middle and leg from Bishoo, the batsman defends it out.
Steps out and mistimes the drive to the man at short extra cover.
These two are looking far more positive now. Dickwella makes room and chops it through the covers for a single.
Pushes it through and the batsman punches it back to Bishoo.
Loopy ball, the batsman goes right across and paddles it away to fine leg for a brace.
Goes wide of the crease and still ends up bowling it pretty wide. Chandimal lets it be. Nine runs from the over, a good one for the visitors.
Bowls it wide outside off and the batsman doesn't play at it.
Roach attacks the stumps and the batsman defends it.

The Windies players are not happy with the ball and it is handed to the umpire, who walks towards his partner at square leg. Time for some trimming, the seam seems to have come off and the scissor is out.
FOUR! Right from the coaching manual! Fuller length ball on off, Chandimal gets a nice stride forward and keeps his balance. He drills it in the gap through the covers. No stopping that one.

FOUR! Flashes and flashes hard! Runs continue to flow from the bat of Chandimal. Short, wide and outside off from Roach. Seeing width, he decides to free his arms. Goes hard at it and gets a thick edge over the slip cordon. The ball goes on the bounce to the third man boundary.
Shortish delivery on the middle and leg stump line, the batsman jumps across and tucks it for a single towards square leg.
Double bowling change from the Windies. Kemar Roach is back on.
Drifts in from outside off, discount spin from it and the batsman pushes it down the track.
The batsman walks across his stumps and flicks it against the spin towards mid-wicket.
Loopy delivery, the batsman gets to the pitch of it and drills it back to Bishoo.
Replica of the previous ball and defended down the track.
Faster leg break on the stumps, Chandimal defends it solidly.
A friendly full toss from Bishoo to start his spell. Dickwella powers it to long on for a single.

Time for some spin! Devendra Bishoo comes into the attack. What does he have up his sleeve? Can he break this stand and open the floodgates for the Windies? Let's wait and see... Jason Holder is having a word with his bowler, he wants to be absolutely sure about the field the leggie wants.
Spears in a full delivery on the stumps, Chandimal plays a defensive stroke off the front foot.
Defends it to covers and looks for a quick single. But this time, the fielder is quick on the ball and he ensures they don't cross over.
Chandimal leans on the front foot and gently pushes it to the cover region.

First sign of aggression by Dickwella! On the pads and the batsman heaves it away to deep square leg. The fielder in the deep rushes to his right and collects it on the bounce. That single brings up the 100 for Sri Lanka.
Bowls it short on the stumps and the batsman defends it back to the bowler.
Works it towards the mid-wicket region and they take another quick single.
Drop and run! They continue to impress with their running! Chandimal hangs back and defends it towards cover-point. Off they go, they complete a single with ease.
Cummins bowls one short and the batsman ducks under it without breaking a sweat.
Shortish delivery, angling down leg. The batsman moves inside the line of it and lets it be.
Short of a length ball, angling in. Chandimal taps it to mid-wicket. He wanted a run but his partner isn't ready.
Moves inside the line of it and tucks it in the gap on the leg side for a single. These two are rotating strike quite regularly, which has been the most impressive part of this partnership.
Shortish delivery and it is angling into the body. Dickwella gently pushes it down the track.
Touch straighter from Holder and the right-hander works it off his pads to deep backward square. They scamper back for the second run. Positive running from the Sri Lankan pair.
Fullish delivery on off, Dinesh leans on the front foot and plays a drive to the man at extra cover.
Too short from Holder, it balloons over the batsman. Luckily for the bowler there is no signal from the umpire.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

Lapse in concentration?  Maybe! In the previous over, Dickwella played a loose shot and now his skipper does the same! Seeing a shortish delivery from Holder, Chandimal tries to cut it a bit too hard and misses it eventually.
Bowls it outside off and the batsman leaves it alone to the keeper.
Another false shot from Dickwella, he played one a few overs back. Chases a wide delivery from Cummins but doesn't make contact with the ball.
Pushes it to cover-point, he wanted the single but his skipper denies.
Good running! This will frustrate the bowler. Chandimal drops it on the leg side and calls for a quick single. He gets a positive response from his partner.
Cummins bangs it in short and pushes the batsman on the back foot. Chandimal bends down and lets it through.

On the pads again and the left-hander tucks it wide of the square leg fielder for a single. 50-run stand between Dickwella and Chandimal. A welcome partnership for Sri Lanka, but the job is not yet done. These two need to focus more as there is no room for complacency in this game.
Slipping it down the leg side, Dickwella looks to flick that but he fails to make contact with the ball. Not collected cleanly by the keeper.
Ends the over with a delivery on the 5th stump channel. The batsman leaves it all alone. These two have added 49 so far.
In the channel outside off, easily left alone by the batsman.
A rising delivery from the bowler, the Lankan skipper gets on top of the bounce and chops it wide of gully. Couple more to Chandimal.
Keeps it fuller this time and attacks the stumps. Chandimal defensively pushes it to silly mid off. This is a lull period of the game, but the Lankan fans won't complain.
In the corridor outside the off stump from Holder and the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Good length ball from Holder, Chandimal hangs back and defends it solidly on the off side.
Pushes it to the left of the mid off fielder and they steal a quick single. Chandimal will retain the strike.
FOUR LEG BYES! Terribly directed by Cummins. He bowls a good length ball down the leg side. Chandimal fails to flick that. The ball brushes the thigh pad and flies past the keeper for a boundary.
Pushes it gently to the mid off region.

Serves up a length ball closer to the off peg, Chandimal defends it. Both the batsmen are focusing on spending time at the crease and not going after the runs, but they have ensured loose balls aren't left unpunished.
Shortish delivery on the off stump line, the batsman hangs back and dabs it to cover-point. It goes straight to the fielder.
Errs in line, steams in and bowls it down the leg side. Chandimal moves across and lets it be.
On the off stump line from Holder, Dickwella pushes it gently to covers.
Dickwella gets right behind that one and defends it solidly down the track.
Loosely played! A widisih delivery from Holder, angling away a little. The batsman plays away from the body and nearly gets an outside edge through to the keeper.
Bowls a short ball to the wicket-keeper batsman. He keeps his hands low and evades it safely.
Touch shorter from the bowler and the batsman eases it on the off side for a single.
Good ball! Tailing in sharply from outside off and it is almost in the blockhole, Chandimal just manages to dig it out towards mid-wicket.
Shortish delivery from Holder, angling in, Chandimal defends it down the track. The Windies skipper has overstepped there, no ball is the signal from the umpire.
Drinks break.
FOUR LEG BYES! This is short and on the pads again. Dickwella fails to put it away. He misses the pull. The ball brushes the pads and goes down to the fine leg fence.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Back of a length on off, Dickwella guides it to point.
Fuller on off, the batsman drives it square on the off side but finds the fielder at point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Slightly shorter on the pads, Chandimal fails to flick it. The ball brushes the pads and goes down to fine leg for a leg bye.
Drifting into the pads of the batsman, who nudges it away to fine leg for a single.
Easy leave for Dinesh Chandimal as that one from the bowler is outside off.
Muted appeal from the Windies player! Holder bowls it on a length, angling down leg, Chandimal gets hit on the pads and there is an appeal which dies down quickly.
Extra lift for the lanky fast bowler. The ball hits the length and jumps up sharply, Chandimal looks to defend that but the ball hits the top of the handle and rolls towards gully.
Dickwella defends a good length ball from Holder to the right of mid off. They take a quick single. Partnership is worth 34 now.
Holder bowls it on a length outside off, Dickwella doesn't play at that one.
The physio is out with the magic spray. Chandimal got hit on the hip bone off the last ball, but he is now good to continue!
Shortish and bowled on the body of the batsman. Chandimal misses the tuck and is hit on the thigh pads.
FOUR! Lovely shot, a very pleasing to the eye that one! Fuller on middle, Chandimal just puts bat to ball and it races away to the long off fence.
Shortish again on middle, Dickwella tucks it towards square leg and gets to the other end.
Goes shorter in length down the leg side. The batsman misses the pull.
Shorter in length and on off, Dickwella defends it to the man at point.
Slightly shorter on middle, Dickwella tucks it to mid-wicket.
Miguel Cummins is brought into the attack.
A little straighter by Holder. Chandimal works it to mid-wicket. A maiden to begin with by the Windies skipper. Not a threatening one though.
Down the leg side. Dinesh misses the flick and it goes into the hands of the keeper.
A little too wide outside off, Dinesh leaves it.
Good length on off, Chandimal is solid in defense.
Back of a length on off, Chandimal goes back and defends it onto the ground.
He too starts off with a loosener. Short and outside off. Chandimal lets it be.
Jason Holder is into the attack for the first time today.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Down the leg side. The batsman misses the flick.
Strays on the pads, Chandimal flicks it down to fine leg for a run.
Goes shorter this time on off, Chandimal blocks it.
Good length on off, Dickwella taps it towards cover for a run. That single also brings up 1000 Test runs for him.
Goes fuller and on middle, Dickwella drives it back to the bowler who does well to go down and stop it with one hand.
Confident push there! Gabriel hits the length again on off. Chandimal gets a nice stride out and punches it through covers for a brace.
Good length on off, Chandimal off the back foot keeps it out.
Goes very full this time on off, Chandimal squeezes it out to point.
Lands it on a length around off, Chandimal defends it awkwardly.
FOUR! Chandimal has looked very good today! This is on the shorter side and outside off, Chandimal makes good use of the depth of the crease and guides it through backward point for a boundary.
Angles this one into the batsman. Chandimal pushes it towards mid on. Roach there scores bull's eye at the non-striker's end but the batsman is well in.
Finishes the over with a decent delivery. On off, Dickwella keeps it out easily.
Gets one right and then again bowls this one way outside off. Niroshan shoulders arms to it.
Better! This time he bowls it on middle, gets it to shape away. Dickwell covers the line and defends it.
Another ball outside off to the left hander by Roach. Dickwella does not play at it. He is getting the ball to swing away but he needs to start from the off or the middle stump line.
Goes short and angles it into the batsman. Chandimal tucks it around the corner for a run.
Fuller in length on off, Chandimal drives it to the man at covers.
Gets it right this time and bowls it on the stumps. Chandimal is solid in defense. The ball rolls towards the cover area and the batsmen steal a run.
No! This is outside off and Dinesh leaves it.

FOUR BYES! That is harsh on the keeper. He had no chance to collect that one. Very wayward from Gabriel. This is way down the leg side. The keeper dives to his left but fails to collect it. It goes down to the fine leg fence. We did see Gabriel bowl one to Mendis yesterday but he then followed it up with a beauty. Can he do the same now?
Goes full and outside off, Shannon wants Chandimal to play a loose stroke there. The Lankan captain, however is determined and resists the temptation. He lets it go through to the keeper

Uppish but safe! Angles this one into the pads. Chandimal tries to flick but it goes off the leading edge towards mid on. Chandimal wanted a run but Dickwella sends him back. Good call by the wicket-keeper batsman. There was never a run there. One thing that the Lankans do not want at the moment is a run out.
Gabriel overpitchs it now but Chandimal drives it straight to the man at covers.

FOUR! Overpitches and pays the price. This is very full on off, Dickwella leans into it and strokes it through covers. The fielder from mid off gives it a chase. He seems to have pulled it back in but the umpires take it upstairs to check and replays confirm he is in contact with the rope as he touches the ball. A boundary signaled.
Another ball which is way outside off, Dickwella need not play at those.

FOUR! Just over the fielder at gully! Full and wide outside off, the sucker ball by Roach. Dickwella cannot resist and he goes after it. The ball takes the outside edge and goes over the fielder for a boundary. 50 comes up for Sri Lanka.
Roach is struggling here against the left hander. He bowls this one way outside off. Dickwella lets it be.

Good shot but it does not get to the boundary! Full and offers width outside off. Chandimal reaches out to it and drives it square on the off side. Bishoo gives it a chase and pulls it back before the crosses the ropes. The batsmen run three.
Fuller and on middle, Chandimal pushes it to mid on.
A bumper to end the over. Dickwella ducks under it.
Bangs this a touch short on the pads, Chandimal misses the flick. The ball hits the pads and rolls towards the square leg region for a leg bye.
Hits the length again on off, Chandimal defends it to the man at point. Tight bowling from Gabriel.
Good length on off, Chandimal gets behind the line and keeps it out.
On the pads of Dickwella, he works it around the corner and gets off the mark.
Fuller and on middle, Chandimal drives it through mid on and collects a run.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Down the leg side, the batsman lets it be.
Another ball outside off, the batsman does not play at it.
The outswinger outside off, left alone.
Niroshan Dickwella is the next man in.

OUT! TIMBER! That was one fast delivery. He comes running in, goes wide of the crease and fires it full. This one shapes back in late. Roshen tries to flick but is a little too late on the shot. He misses and the ball clips his front pad and goes onto uproot the leg stump. An early wicket this morning for the Windies and the Lankans slip further. They trail by another 371.
Gets the ball to tail back in but the line is a touch straighter. Roshen is hit on the pads as he tries to flick it.

FOUR BYES! Plenty of bounce and pace on that delivery! It is way too short. The batsman lets it be and Dowrich behind the stumps tries to collect it with a leap but fails to do so. So a good start for Sri Lanka here. Three boundaries in the first two overs.
Closer to the off pole but not close enough to make the batsman play at it.
Back of a length outside off, Chandimal does the right thing. He does not offer a stroke to it.
Ahead of a length this time on the off stump. Chandimal is solid in defense.
Drags his length back and bowls it a touch outside off. Chandimal stands tall and shoulders arms to it.
FOUR! Excellent start for the Sri Lanka skipper! A boundary to begin. Full and on the pads, a wrong ball with a strong off side field. Chandimal works it through mid on and the ball races away.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl from the other end.

A peach to end the over! Once again he goes wide of the crease and creates problems for the batsman. Angles it in and then gets it to straighten. This one also stays low. Roshen tries to keep it out but gets beaten.
Another ball outside off, left alone.
FOUR! First runs today is in the form of a boundary! This was a touch fuller by Roach on off, no movement for him. Easy for Silva as he leans into it and strokes it through mid off.
Another outswinger but the line is not right. It is outside off. Roshen does not fiddle with it.
A beauty to follow up the loosener! Roach goes wide of the crease and angles it into the off stump. It pitches and leaves the batsman. Silva tries to keep it out but is beaten by the away movement.
Starts off with a loosener outside off. The batsman need not play at those.

We are all set for the action to begin. The players make their way out to the middle. Dinesh Chandimal and Roshen Silva will resume their innings. The latter will be on strike and he will be facing Kemar Roach who will start the proceedings for today. He has three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

Hello and welcome to Day 3. West Indies fought brilliantly yesterday and they find themselves in the driver's seat. The visiting team still trail by a big margin and only have seven wickets in hand. They need healthy contributions from the rest of the batters, if they are to get anywhere close to the total posted by the Windies. On the other hand, the home team will look to take more wickets with the red cherry which is relatively new and continue their domination. An action-packed day awaits us. Do stay tuned as the drama unfolds.
... Day 3, Session 1...

Earlier in the day, Dowrich showed great application with the bat and he was ably supported by the lower-order batsmen which helped the home team get to a massive first innings score. Sri Lankan bowling looked toothless and they even failed to stop the run flow. Overall, the day belonged to the hosts who won all the three sessions today and have a firm grip on this game. Friday will be a big one for the visitors. The batters need to apply themselves to get their team out of trouble. Whereas, West Indies will want more of what happened in the final hour on Day 2. Join us to find out what Day 3 holds for us at 1000 local (1400 GMT). Adios!

At 16 for 2 all the onus of getting Sri Lanka back into the game was on the shoulders of their two experienced batters, Chandimal and Mathews. They took a few blows and tried to see off the turbulent phase. The latter even got a reprieve off the first ball but he failed to make it count as he fell prey to the West Indian skipper who had dropped him. Roshen Silva did walk out to bat for a handful of deliveries before the umpire offered light to the batsmen.

The light has been offered to the batsmen and it is not a surprise that they have taken it. Off come the bails of the grid and that will be STUMPS ON DAY 2! It was a testing little session for the Sri Lankan batsmen and they have failed the litmus test. They simply had no answers to what the West Indian pacers threw at them. The away team's innings started on a poor note as Kusal Perera gifted his wicket to Roach on the very first ball he faced. Gabriel, who was a touch wayward, produced a beauty to get rid of the other opener.
Short of a length ball outside off, nipping in a little but Chandimal sits back and leaves it confidently.
Touch straight, Roshen moves inside the line of it and tucks it to square leg for a single.

Another outside edge, but it falls lands well short of the man at first slip. A good length delivery from Holder, jumps sharply and moves away a little, Roshen looks to defend that but gets a thick edge behind.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Roshen Silva is the next man in.

OUT! Holder has just got something behind the line. From one angle it looked like there was nothing behind the line, but the third umpire thinks otherwise. Jason makes amends for dropping Mathews by getting his wicket. It's a lovely outswinger from the Windies skipper, as he pitches it on a perfect length around the off stump. The batsman HAD TO PLAY AT IT. The ball catches the outside edge and flies low between second and third slip. Roston Chase from the latter position moves to his left and takes a wonderful catch. Jason and his players start to celebrate but the umpire wants to check whether the bowler has overstepped. The television umpire sees a few replays and eventually deems it legitimate. Sri Lanka have lost their third and they are now staring down the barrel.
Mathews is caught at third slip, but the umpire wants to check for the front foot no ball. Has Holder overstepped? Will be a marginal call.

FOUR! SMACKED IT! That will release some pressure which was mounting on the Sri Lankan pair! An innocuous delivery from Holder on a length outside off. Mathews sits back and slams it through the covers for a boundary.
Jason Holder comes into the attack.
Effort ball to end the over. Attacks the body with a shortish delivery, Chandimal stands tall and keeps it out.
In the channel outside off and the batsman is content in leaving those.
Keeps batsman on the back foot with a short of a length ball. Chandimal pushes to covers.
Shortish delivery outside off, the batsman is happy to leave those.
Punched off the back foot through point. Bishoo chases it and keeps it down to two.
Serves up a good length ball outside off, Chandimal decides to leave it.

FOUR! Wow, fine shot from Mathews! Shortish delivery from Gabriel, doesn't rise as much as Mathews anticipated. But he adjusts quickly and pulls it with authority towards the vacant mid-wicket region and earns a boundary.

Chadimal is off the mark with the 24th delivery he faces. He gets a delivery slightly wider and pushes it wide of the man at cover-point for a single. He will feel pretty confident after registering his first run.
Relatively easy leave for Dinesh Chandimal.

Unplayable delivery from Gabriel! As a batsman all you need to do is to forget it and focus on the next one. Good length ball, swings away at the last moment. Chandimal looks to defend that but he is beaten on the outside edge.
Angling in from outside off and ends up closer to the off peg. Well left by Chandimal.
Eases it wide of the man at short extra cover and gets down to the other end with a brisk single.
Slightly wider and the batsman decides to leave that one.

Now, that's a loose shot from the Sri Lankan skipper. Pressure telling on him. He gets a widish delivery which should have been put away. Goes after it but fails to connect as he lost his shape while attempting a square cut.
Short of a length ball, Chandimal defends it out. 18 dots so far for the right-hander.
Awkwardly played. Bowls it short on the rib cage of the batsman, who hops across and nudges it an unconvincing manner to fine leg for a single.
Follows it up with a lively delivery, rising high. Mathews hangs back and defends it down the track.
Good carry through to the keeper. Bowls it on the shorter side and the batsman lets it go. The keeper collects it above his shoulders.
Miguel Cummins into the attack, replacing Kemar Roach.
Length ball outside off, Chandimal covers his stumps and lets it through to Dowrich.
This is clever cricket from Mathews, he gets off strike with a quick single. Drops the ball on the off side and calls for a run. He gets a positive response from his partner.
Bangs it in short on off, Mathews powers it to backward point but can't find the gap.
Mathews hangs on the back foot and fends it awkwardly on to the off side.

Thunderbolt from Gabriel! Another pacey, shortish delivery, zooms in at pace. A good delivery and equally well-played by Mathews. He keeps his hands low and sways away from the line of it. The keeper gets a hand to it and takes pace off it. The fielder from the slip cordon runs to the ball and prevents the single.
The physio once again comes out to the middle. Checking for any possible concussion. Mathews though now seems fine to continue.

OH BOY!!! A snorter! Earlier, Chandimal took a blow on the elbow and now, Mathews gets hit on the helmet. A short ball from Gabriel, it is well-directed towards the batsman, who looks to get out of the way but gets hit on the helmet.
In the similar zone and it gets the similar response from the batter.
On a good length ball outside off, angling in, the batsman decides to leave it.
Chandimal seems to be in a lot of pain and the physio rushes out onto the middle with the magic spray. Sri Lankan fans will hope that it is not a serious blow.

OUCH! That is pretty nasty! Short of a length ball, rearing up at pace. Chandimal hangs back and looks to defend that but the ball rises sharply and hits him on the right elbow. He straightaway shows some discomfort and moves away from the stumps.
The Sri Lankan skipper uses his wrists and flicks it on the leg side. He wanted a run but Mathews isn't ready for it.
Angling in from outside off and Chandimal defends it solidly.
On a length outside off, Chandimal decides to leave that one.

Beauty! Comes in from over the wicket and it straightens after pitching, the ball whizzes past the outside edge as Mathews looks to defend that. End of an action-packed over by Gabriel, 10 runs, a wicket and a dropped catch from it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Dropped by Holder! This game is such a leveler! He grabbed a beauty in the previous ball and drops a relatively simple chance this time. Reprieve off the very first ball for Mathews. How costly will this prove? We do know how good a player he is. He gets a good length ball outside off, swings away a little and the batsman looks to push that on the off side. He gets a thick edge to third slip, where Holder gets both the hands to it but fails to pouch it.
Angelo Mathews is the next man in.

OUT! The Television Umpire is happy with what he has seen, gives it in the favor of the hosts and Mendis gets his marching orders. It is an excellent catch from the West Indian skipper. Coming to the ball - Gabriel dishes out a pacey delivery on a good length, which skids through after pitching. Mendis goes on the back foot and jabs at it with hard hands. The ball catches the outside edge and goes low to third slip, where Holder seems to have taken a good catch. He is pretty confident and claims it straightaway. However, the umpires play safe and send the case to their mate upstairs. Replays roll in and they are conclusive enough for the TV umpire to reckon it is out. Sri Lanka have lost one of their most talented young players and are in big trouble here.
Did that carry? Jason Holder is pretty confident and the players from the home team are celebrating. Soft signal from Aleem Dar is OUT.
Shortish delivery on off, Mendis stands tall and pushes it on the off side.

FIVE Wides! Wayward stuff from Gabriel, he bowls from wide of the crease, well down the leg side and it angles further away. Poor Dowrich has no chance of stopping it. Five bonus runs gift wrapped to Sri Lanka.
Back of a length ball outside off, Mendis shoulders arms to it.

No ball! and FOUR Leg byes. Gabriel steams in and bowls it down the leg side. Mendis is late on it. The ball hits the thigh pad and races away to the fine leg fence. No ball is the signal from Aleem Dar, but the replays show it was a harsh call. Gabriel did have something behind the line which the umpire missed.
Keeps it fuller and it brings the batsman on the front foot. Chandimal defends it solidly down the track.
Angling in from outside off, Chandimal goes back and pushes it to covers. Nine dots for the Sri Lankan skipper so far.
Short of a length ball outside off, Chandimal lifts his bat and shoulders arms to it.
Misses his target and dishes out a delivery down the leg side, the batsman lets it go.
That one shoots through! A seam up delivery, hits the pitch and keeps pretty low, Chanidmal goes back to defend that but the ball sneaks under his bat. Signs of unevenness? Oh yes.
Bowls from wide of the crease, and way outside off. Chandimal doesn't offer a stroke to it.
Angles this one into the batsman. Mendis defends it solidly. A brilliant and pacey first over by Gabriel comes to an end. Also no no balls from him. Excellent!
BEATEN FOR PACE! What a jaffa that was. On a length and around off, this one straightens. Mendis tries to get his bat done but the ball whizzes past the outside edge and to the keeper.
Good bumper there! That was quick and a well-directed one. Mendis does well to evade it.
FOUR! Off the mark in style! Short ball and on off, Mendis opens the face of the bat, uses the pace and guides it through backward point for a boundary.
Beauty! This is on a length and around off, this one shapes away. Mendis prods forward and tries to defend but gets beaten.
He bowls a good length ball first up on middle. It comes back in after pitching. Mendis tries to work it on the leg side but misses to get hit on the pads.
Shannon Gabriel will bowl from the other end.
Another length ball on off, Chandimal defends it. End of a wayward first over but a successful one by Roach.
On a length and this one rises after pitching. Dinesh does well to play it down onto the ground with soft hands.
Another ball outside off, Dinesh makes another leave.
Another ball wide outside off, Chandimal does what Perera should have. LEAVES IT.
Dinesh Chandimal is the next man in.

OUT! Caught! Kusal Perera bags a golden duck. Not a good return into the Test team for him. A poor shot to be honest. Not what you want to be playing on your first ball. A full ball outside off, way outside off I should say. Perera should have left it alone but he says, I need no sighters and goes after it. The ball hits the toe end and lobs towards Chase at point who takes it easily. An early strike for the Windies and they are all over the Sri Lankan team at the moment.

WIDE! Swing for Roach but there was no control in that delivery. This was full and way outside off, swinging away further. It bounces just in front of the keeper who fails to collect it. He does get a glove to it and goes down towards third man for a bye.
Starts off with a good length ball on off, Mendis defends it off the front foot.
